headline: Adopted a five-year Central Square Technologies contract; granted National Grid conduit permits on four streets; referred proposed rules 61-63 to committee.
summary: Members approved a five-year Central Square Technologies contract and advertised 25 ordinances tied to amendments to the Salary Ordinance. They also approved $47,836.54 for prior year Public Works invoices and granted National Grid conduit permits on four streets. Proposed Rules 61, 62, and 63 and a review of meeting start times were sent to committee by split votes.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 29, 2026 meeting, 11-0.
Approved National Grid conduit permit at Chadwick St., 11-0.
Approved National Grid conduit permit at Franklin St. and Arctic St., 11-0.
Approved National Grid conduit permit at Grafton St., 11-0.
Approved National Grid conduit permit at Pleasant St., 11-0.
Referred Asaad Challab's request for an 85-foot sewer extension to Public Works Committee, 11-0.
Referred four traffic and parking requests to Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Voted to advertise 25 ordinances tied to amendments to the Salary Ordinance, 11-0.
Adopted the Central Square Technologies five-year contract, 11-0.
Referred ALERTWorcester enrollment numbers report to Public Safety.
Referred proposed Council Rules 61, 62, and 63 to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 10-1.
Referred Zero Waste Master Plan communication to Urban Technologies, Innovation and Environment Committee, 11-0.
Authorized $47,836.54 from Public Works cost centers to pay prior year invoices, 11-0.
Referred school safety audit to Education Committee and Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Approved an increase in the COLA maximum base from $16,000 to $17,000 starting July 1, 2027, 11-0.
Referred the order on meeting start times and public participation to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, as amended, 8-3.
Adopted request that City Manager ensure students get notice about pedestrian safety measures near schools, 11-0.
Referred review of Rule Five on calling special meetings to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 8-3.
